target_moa.text: Fixed-dose combination: elvitegravir is an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor; emtricitabine and tenofovir DF are nucleoside/nucleotide analogues that inhibit HIV-1 reverse transcriptase; cobicistat is a mechanism-based CYP3A inhibitor that pharmacokinetically boosts elvitegravir.

citations.quote: EVG is an integrase strand-transfer inhibitor that functions by preventing integration of HIV-1 genetic material into the host cell genome.
FTC and TDF (a nucleoside analogue of cytidine and nucleotide analogue of adenosine monophosphate respectively) function by inhibiting the HIV-1 reverse transcriptase.
Cobicistat is a mechanism-based inhibitor of cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes of the CYP3A family.

modality.text: Small molecule fixed-dose combination tablet (elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, tenofovir DF)

citations.quote: STRIBILD is a fixed-dose combination tablet containing elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were nausea (16%) and diarrhea (12%). Safety based on 1408 subjects. Key identified risks include new onset/worsening renal impairment and proximal renal tubulopathy (the cobicistat component has been shown to increase serum creatinine due to inhibition of tubular secretion of creatinine without affecting renal glomerular function; elevation in serum creatinine occurred in 7% of STRIBILD subjects vs 1% ATRIPLA and 4% ATV/r+TRUVADA) and decreases in bone mineral density.

citations.quote: Table 2 displays the frequency of adverse drug reactions greater than or equal to 5%.
Nausea	16%	9%	13%
Diarrhea	12%	11%	16%

The safety assessment of STRIBILD is based on pooled data from 1408 subjects in two comparative clinical trials, Study 102 and Study 103, in antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV-1 infected adult subjects.

The following adverse reactions, listed under the body system headings above, may occur as a consequence of proximal renal tubulopathy: rhabdomyolysis, osteomalacia, hypokalemia, muscular weakness, myopathy, hypophosphatemia.

The cobicistat component of STRIBILD has been shown to increase serum creatinine and decrease estimated creatinine clearance due to inhibition of tubular secretion of creatinine without affecting renal glomerular function. In Studies 102 and 103, increases in serum creatinine and decreases in estimated creatinine clearance occurred early in treatment with STRIBILD, after which they stabilized. The
Elevation in serum creatinine (all grades) occurred in 7% of subjects receiving STRIBILD, 1% of subjects receiving ATRIPLA, and 4% of subjects receiving atazanavir + ritonavir + TRUVADA.

detail.text: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS/SEVERE HEPATOMEGALY WITH STEATOSIS and POST TREATMENT ACUTE EXACERBATION OF HEPATITIS B. Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis, including fatal cases, have been reported with nucleoside analogs including tenofovir DF; severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in HBV/HIV-1 coinfected patients who discontinued products containing emtricitabine or tenofovir DF.

requirement.text: 1919-7: Perform a clinical trial (approximately 500 women) to characterize incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women, with a renal monitoring algorithm similar to that used in GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103.

citations.quote: 1919-7 Perform a clinical trial to better characterize the incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women. Provide adequate renal monitoring in the proposed trial to assess renal safety employing a renal monitoring algorithm similar to that used in GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103. The algorithm will include an assessment of serum creatinine, creatinine clearance by Cockcroft-Gault, glomerular filtration rate (GFR) by cystatin C, serum phosphate, renal phosphate threshold (TmP/GFR), urine protein and urine glucose. The trial will enroll approximately 500 women, in order to assess the relative incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women as compared to men enrolled in other Stribild clinical trials.

summary.text: NDA 203100 for the STRIBILD (E/C/F/T) fixed-dose combination was submitted/received October 27, 2011 and reviewed under standard review with a PDUFA goal date of August 27, 2012. The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee met May 11, 2012 and voted 13-1 that the data support approval. Approval was based on two Phase 3 non-inferiority trials (GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103) demonstrating virologic success at Week 48 (traditional approval, not accelerated); the application was approved first cycle on August 27, 2012 with multiple postmarketing requirements and no REMS.
